Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Inc. third quarter fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Inc.'s results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer; Casey Nguyen, VP of Sales; Riley Brooks, Chief Marketing Officer; and Alex Chen, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. CyberShield Inc. delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of our CNAPP platform is accelerating, demonstrating the critical impact in securing multi-cloud environments and the unmatched value we bring to our customers.

Our strategic priorities are focused on eight key areas: the performance of our key product lines like cloud security and SASE, the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy, market share trends, the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue, billings performance versus guidance, channel partner performance and their contribution to revenue, details on recent product and feature launches, and expansion within existing large accounts.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We achieved record revenue of $520 million in the third quarter, representing a 38% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $320 million. Net income was $95 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.72. We are increasing our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'll now dive into the performance of our key product lines, with a particular focus on Cloud Security and SASE—two pillars driving our record Q3 results. As you know, these segments represent over 65% of our total ARR, which grew 38% year-over-year to $2.4 billion, outpacing the broader cybersecurity market's 15-20% growth as reported by Gartner and IDC.

Starting with Cloud Security, this segment delivered exceptional results, posting $850 million in quarterly revenue—a 48% increase YoY and 12% quarter-over-quarter. ARR in this line hit $3.2 billion, up 52% YoY, fueled by accelerating cloud migrations and the multi-cloud sprawl that's become the new normal. Our CNAPP platform, which integrates CSPM, CWPP, and DSPM functionalities, was the star performer, accounting for 60% of segment revenue and growing 65% YoY. We've seen strong adoption among Fortune 500 enterprises shifting workloads to AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud—think integrations with AWS Bedrock for GenAI security and Azure Arc for hybrid environments.

Key trends here include the explosion in cloud-native threats: we've blocked over 1.2 billion malicious API calls in Q3 alone via our runtime protection engine, a 75% increase from last year, driven by AI-powered supply chain attacks reminiscent of the SolarWinds incident. Customer metrics underscore this momentum—net retention rate climbed to 128%, with expansions into data security posture management adding $150 million in upsell ARR. Notable wins include a top-5 hyperscaler expanding our platform to secure their sovereign cloud offerings and a major financial services firm in EMEA adopting our CNAPP to comply with DORA regulations.

Regionally, Americas led with 55% YoY growth, propelled by ransomware surges—up 30% per Chainalysis data—while APAC surged 62% on digital transformation in Japan and India, where we've partnered with NTT for localized threat intelligence. EMEA grew 40%, though supply chain delays in CSPM sensor deployments tempered upside by 2-3 points. Strategically, we're doubling down on zero-trust cloud architectures with our CloudShield AI initiative, leveraging ML models trained on 500 petabytes of telemetry to achieve 99.9% accuracy in anomaly detection, ahead of peers like Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud or Wiz. R&D investment here rose 25% QoQ to $120 million, positioning us for 50%+ growth in FY'25 as Gartner predicts the CNAPP market hitting $15 billion by 2027.

Moving to SASE, our fastest-growing segment, revenue reached $620 million—up a stellar 62% YoY and 18% QoQ—with ARR surpassing $2.1 billion, a 68% increase. This reflects the ongoing convergence of networking and security, accelerated by hybrid work: 85% of our new SASE logos cited remote/branch access as the primary driver, per our post-sale surveys. Our SecureNet SASE platform, bundling SD-WAN, ZTNA, SWG, CASB, and DLP, now secures 15 million global endpoints, processing 50 trillion sessions quarterly with sub-50ms latency—critical for SSE in bandwidth-constrained regions.

Performance highlights include a 135% YoY ramp in ZTNA modules, outpacing Zscaler's 40% growth per their last earnings, thanks to our Adaptive Trust engine that dynamically enforces least-privilege access using behavioral biometrics and UEBA. We added 450 net new customers, including a hyperscale telco in LATAM and a European auto OEM migrating from legacy VPNs. Churn remains elite at under 2% annualized, with gross retention at 98%, bolstered by our single-pane-of-glass console that reduced MTTR by 40% for breach response.

Regionally, APAC was the powerhouse at 75% YoY growth, driven by 5G rollouts in Southeast Asia and partnerships with Singtel—offsetting softer macro in China due to regulatory scrutiny on data flows. Americas grew 58%, fueled by federal SASE mandates under CISA's Zero Trust Maturity Model, while EMEA hit 50% amid NIS2 compliance waves. A minor headwind: competitive pricing pressure from Cato Networks shaved 1-2 points off margins, now at 82% gross—still top-tier.

Strategically, we're accelerating SASE innovation with SASE 2.0, embedding GenAI for autonomous threat hunting—early pilots show 60% faster playbook execution versus CrowdStrike's Falcon platform. We've earmarked $200 million for FY'25 M&A, eyeing FWaaS bolt-ons to challenge Netskope, and expanded our channel ecosystem, now 45% of bookings via hyperscaler marketplaces like AWS Marketplace, up from 30%.

In summary, Cloud Security and SASE are not just growing—they're redefining our competitive moat in a $200 billion TAM expanding at 16% CAGR per IDC. These lines achieved 95% of their non-GAAP operating margin expansion, contributing 300 basis points to group margins at 29%. We're confident in our guide for 45-50% segment growth in Q4, underpinned by a $4.2 billion backlog.

As we dive into the financials further, I'd like to spend some time on one of our key growth drivers: the effectiveness of our go-to-market, or GTM, strategy. In the cybersecurity industry, where threats evolve faster than ever—think the 300% surge in ransomware incidents reported by Chainalysis this year and the relentless push toward zero-trust architectures—our GTM has been laser-focused on delivering scalable, high-velocity sales motions while maintaining disciplined unit economics. We've structured it around three pillars: direct enterprise sales, channel partnerships, and product-led growth via our SaaS platform, with targeted investments in AI-enhanced inbound marketing and vertical-specific solutions.

Let me start with the headline metrics, which underscore the strategy's resounding success. New logo ARR contributed significantly to growth, reflecting our ability to penetrate new accounts amid a frosty macro environment. Customer Acquisition Cost payback has compressed to just 9 months from 12 months a year ago, thanks to optimized sales cycles averaging 85 days—down from 110—and a stellar 28% win rate on qualified opportunities, outperforming our peer average of 22% per Forrester's latest Enterprise Sales Index.

On the channel front, we've doubled down on our partner ecosystem, which now drives a substantial portion of total bookings. Strategic alliances with hyperscalers like AWS Marketplace and Azure, alongside VARs such as CDW and Insight Enterprises, have been game-changers. We've also seen strong attach rates for our managed detection and response add-on, boosting average annual contract value per enterprise deal.

Product-led growth remains a differentiator in our mid-market segment. Our freemium trial has converted at rates more than double the industry SaaS benchmark, driving self-serve ARR. This PLG flywheel is amplified by technical initiatives like our Zero Trust Network Access 2.0 release, which integrates seamlessly with SIEM leaders like Splunk and Elastic Stack. Early adopters report 40% faster threat remediation times, directly correlating to a 92% Net Revenue Retention rate—well above the cybersecurity sector median cited by Bessemer Venture Partners.

Regionally, our GTM is tailored to local dynamics. In North America, enterprise logos grew strongly, anchored by hyperscale deals in financial services and healthcare. We've capitalized on post-Log4Shell regulatory tailwinds, closing large deals with banks adopting our AI-driven deception technology to counter advanced persistent threats. EMEA delivered robust growth, propelled by NIS2 Directive compliance demands; partnerships with local MSSPs have accelerated our ramp. APAC is our fastest grower, thanks to data center launches supporting local regs. China expansions via joint ventures mirror successful playbooks, while India hyperscaler deals tap the cloud security spend growth per IDC.

Strategically, we're ahead of key industry trends: the shift to consolidated platforms amid SASE fatigue, where single-vendor stacks like ours reduce complexity versus point solutions. Our upsell/cross-sell ratio is strong, driven by adoption of our Cloud Workload Protection Platform among existing EDR customers, addressing the rise in container vulnerabilities flagged by Sysdig's report. Churn remains sub-2% annually, with expansion ARR exceeding retained revenue.

Looking ahead, we're allocating incremental resources to GTM, split between sales capacity in APAC, AI-powered account-based marketing targeting CISOs, and channel incentives. This positions us for continued ARR growth, with strong Rule of 40 scoring. Early pipeline signals show solid coverage for Q4, diversified across verticals.

I'll now turn to our market share trends, which continue to underscore CyberShield Inc.'s leadership position in the $200 billion-plus cybersecurity market. The industry is experiencing robust tailwinds, with IDC projecting a 13.5% CAGR through 2027, driven by escalating ransomware attacks—up 65% YoY per our threat intelligence report—geopolitical cyber threats, and the relentless shift to hybrid cloud environments. We've capitalized on these dynamics through our AI-powered platform, CyberShield Sentinel, which integrates EDR, XDR, and SASE capabilities into a unified zero-trust architecture.

According to the latest Gartner Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms, CyberShield has maintained its Visionary status and climbed to a top position overall, surpassing key competitors and closing the gap with leaders. In terms of global market share across our core segments—endpoint security, cloud workload protection, and network detection—we've expanded significantly year-over-year, per our internal analysis corroborated by Forrester Wave data. This represents substantial YoY increase in share, outpacing the market's overall growth.

Diving into segments: Endpoint Detection and Response remains our fortress, with commanding share gains. Key wins include net-new Fortune 1000 logos, such as a major U.S. bank migrating due to our superior behavioral AI, which boasts high true positive rates and faster MTTR in MITRE ATT&CK evaluations. We've also seen strong uptake of modules embedding runtime application self-protection to counter supply chain vulnerabilities.

Cloud Security Posture Management and Workload Protection: We've surged ahead, fueled by integrations with major cloud providers. Our cloud-native CNAPP has captured significant mid-market share, with deployments replacing competitors. This growth is propelled by ML-driven anomaly detection reducing false positives.

Secure Access Service Edge: An emerging bright spot with sharp share gains, as organizations consolidate vendors. We've edged out rivals in RFPs by offering converged SASE with embedded deception technology.

Regionally: North America dominant, with gains from federal wins. EMEA steady but challenged by regs, offset by growth in key markets via MSSPs focusing on OT security. APAC fastest-growing, driven by mandates and partnerships. LATAM nascent but gaining traction.

Strategically, these gains stem from R&D reinvestment—launching Quantum-Resistant Encryption ahead of NIST; M&A bolstering API security; and customer-centric metrics with high NPS, gross retention, and net expansion.

Looking ahead, we expect further share gains by doubling down on GenAI security and identity threat detection. Our lower TCO and single-pane console give us an edge.

Before diving deeper, I want to address a key factor influencing our reported results: the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations on revenue. As a global leader, we derive approximately 45% of revenue from international markets. This exposure introduces volatility from currency movements.

In Q3, currency fluctuations represented a headwind of about 3% relative to constant currency growth. Reported revenue grew 38%, but at constant FX, it would have been higher—highlighting the strength of our ARR. Billings similarly affected, but RPO strong with multi-year contracts.

Regionally: EMEA bore the brunt from euro depreciation; APAC from yen and AUD swings; Americas minimal; ROW limited drag.

This aligns with market dynamics: DXY surge exacerbating headwinds for USD reporters. Demand inelastic amid rising spend.

Mitigations: Hedging covering 75% exposure; natural hedges and local pricing; diversification; AI-powered forecasting.

Forward-looking, we expect volatility but guide to strong growth at constant currency.

I'll now turn to our billings performance, which came in at $428 million, representing 28% year-over-year growth and 8% sequential, exceeding the high end of guidance by 3%. This outperformance underscores accelerating demand amid ransomware surges and zero-trust shifts.

Billings serve as a leading indicator; revenue recognized $372 million, deferred $1.82 billion up 32% YoY. cRPO $1.45 billion up 35%, total RPO $2.91 billion up 38%. Net retention 118%.

Drivers: New logo ACV strong from bundling EDR, CWP, SASE; expansions from GenAI modules outperforming MITRE; multi-year deals 62%.

Regionally balanced: North America strong on federal; EMEA robust; APAC tempered but rebounding; LATAM growing.

Validates platformization; guiding Q4 higher, raising FY outlook.

I'd like to dive deeper into our channel partner ecosystem and its outsized contribution to revenue. Channel partners—VARs, MSPs, SIs, distributors like TD SYNNEX—represent the backbone, driving 68% of total revenue, $285 million out of $420 million quarterly top line, up 32% YoY, exceeding industry average.

Top-tier partners generated 82%, with larger deal sizes from bundles. Lower tiers grew faster in SMB.

Trends: SASE surged 55% partner-attached; XDR upsell 41%.

Regional: Americas 52% on federal/ransomware; EMEA 28% on NIS2; APAC 20% on mandates.

Enablement: Training platform, incentive program boosting NPS.

Ahead: Integrations, targeting higher mix.

Finally, expansion within existing large accounts—over $1M ARR, 65% base—hit $52 million, 37% of new ARR, driving DBNR to 131%, 11th straight quarter strong. Pure expansion 142%.

Drivers: Multi-product to 4.7 modules avg; land-expand with TAMs; ZTNA attach.

Regional: NA 137%, EMEA 128%, APAC 119%.

Capitalizing on cloud/AI/reg trends; bundling, integrations.

Q4 pipeline $210 million; guiding 130-132% FY DBNR.

With that, I'll turn it back to Alex for additional perspectives.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Jordan, for that comprehensive overview.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. Our technology team is focused on developing cutting-edge security solutions that leverage the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. We're pushing boundaries in market share trends through innovations like our AI-powered Sentinel platform, maintaining top Gartner positions and gaining ground in EDR, cloud security, and SASE with superior MITRE results and integrations that deliver unmatched anomaly detection and response times.

Morgan Patel: Security remains our top priority. We are continuously monitoring the threat landscape—ransomware up 65%, nation-state APTs, supply chain risks—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure with zero-trust architectures and real-time threat hunting.

Casey Nguyen: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with our customers and partners, driving high win rates and efficient cycles through our effective GTM, with pipeline coverage supporting continued outperformance.

Riley Brooks: Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. We are using a variety of channels to reach our target audience, including digital marketing, public relations, and events. We are also investing in thought leadership initiatives to establish CyberShield as a trusted advisor in the cybersecurity industry.

Alex Chen: Thank you. Our product strategy focuses on delivering innovative and integrated security solutions that address the evolving needs of our customers. We are constantly gathering feedback from our customers and partners to ensure that our products meet their needs and exceed their expectations. I'm thrilled to dive into the details of our recent product and feature launches, which have been pivotal in driving our record Q3 results. At CyberShield Inc., we've always prioritized innovation at the intersection of AI-driven threat intelligence, zero-trust architectures, and cloud-native security. In the past two quarters, we've executed on three major launches that not only address the escalating cyber threats—ransomware incidents up 93% YoY per Chainalysis' 2024 report—but also capitalize on the $215 billion global cybersecurity market projected to grow at 13.8% CAGR through 2030, according to Gartner.

Let me start with our flagship launch: CyberShield XDR Elite, our next-generation Extended Detection and Response platform. Building on our core EDR foundation, XDR Elite integrates autonomous AI agents for cross-domain threat hunting across endpoints, networks, cloud workloads, and SaaS applications. What sets it apart is our proprietary NeuroShield AI engine, which leverages federated learning from over 15 petabytes of anonymized telemetry data across thousands of enterprise customers. This enables real-time anomaly detection with a 98.7% true positive rate and under 2-second mean time to respond—a 40% improvement over our prior version and outperforming competitors like CrowdStrike's Falcon XDR, where industry benchmarks from MITRE Engenuity show average MTTRs of 5-7 seconds.

Since launch, XDR Elite has generated substantial new ARR bookings, representing a significant portion of Q3 total. Customer adoption has been explosive: we've onboarded hundreds of new logos, including Fortune 500 names in financial services. Regionally, North America leads, fueled by CISA's zero-trust mandates. EMEA growing amid GDPR; APAC fastest at high YoY rates, with telco bundles.

This positions us to capture share in the XDR market. We've also introduced upsell programs converting EDR to XDR, boosting net retention well above industry averages.

Moving to our converged SASE platform, CyberShield SecureEdge, unifying SD-WAN, ZTNA, CASB, and FWaaS into a single, AI-orchestrated pane of glass. In a world where most enterprises are hybrid/multi-cloud, SecureEdge addresses secure access with Quantum-Resistant Key Exchange compliant with NIST standards. This future-proofs against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.

Beta trials showed 89% reduction in lateral movement risks and 99.999% uptime. Post-GA, strong ARR contribution, high attach rates. Sales cycles shortened thanks to integrations.

APAC leads bookings, NA strong via marketplaces, EMEA with localized DCs.

Challenges leaders with lower TCO; new patents on microsegmentation.

Finally, features like RansomVault Prevent detecting double-extortion pre-encryption at 96% rates; SBOM Guardian for vuln scanning.

These have supercharged our funnel: pipeline up 62% QoQ. Churn sub-2%, net expansion 132%. Targeting major revenue from innovations, R&D up.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press * then 1 to ask a question. Our first question comes from Mike Harris with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Harris: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, could you expand on the cloud security and SASE performance, especially regional variances and how that informs Q4 guide?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Mike. As detailed, Cloud Security saw 48% YoY with Americas at 55%, APAC 62%, EMEA 40%. SASE even stronger at 62%, APAC 75%, Americas 58%. These trends, plus $4.2B backlog, underpin our 45-50% Q4 segment growth confidence despite minor headwinds.

Operator: Next question from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great results. On billings beating guidance and the raised FY outlook—what were the biggest surprises there, and any FX assumptions baked in?

Jordan Lee: Lisa, thanks. Billings $428M beat by $13M from new logos $112M up 42%, expansions $186M up 26%, multi-year 62%. Regional strength across NA 31%, EMEA 29%. FY billings now $1.72B-$1.74B, revenue $1.48B-$1.49B, assuming moderate FX headwind of $50-70M full-year.

Operator: Next from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel: Taylor, impressive tech momentum. How are recent launches like XDR Elite positioning you against MITRE results and GenAI threats?

Taylor Kim: David, thanks. Our NeuroShield AI in XDR Elite delivers 98.7% TPR, 2-sec MTTR—top-tier MITRE alongside leaders. For GenAI, Guardrail blocks 98% prompt injections; Quantum-Resistant ahead of NIST. Driving share gains to 18% targeted FY25.

Operator: Final question from Emma Ruiz with Barclays.

Emma Ruiz: Morgan, with ransomware and APTs surging, how is your threat intel feeding product roadmaps, especially expansions?

Morgan Patel: Emma, spot on. Our telemetry blocks 1.2B API calls Q3, up 75%; Adaptive Trust in SASE cuts churn via UEBA. Large account DBNR 131% from layering GenAI Hunter, OT/IoT—expansions $52M Q3, pipeline $210M Q4.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
